subject: Clarify audit sampling plan, pen-test staging access, and evidence handback schedule
messages:
From: James Sullivan <j.sullivan@acmehealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify audit rights / pen-test window for Redwood MSA

Hi Grace,

We're almost ready to sign the MSA + Order Form but need to lock down two things in the security exhibit before legal will approve:

1) Penetration test windows — Acme prefers 2-week windows per quarter and a staging-only rule (no production tests). Is that compatible with Redwood's current ops constraints?

2) Audit sampling / evidence cadence — we need a clear commitment on SOC 2 evidence snapshots (evidence cadence, who owns export). Our compliance team typically asks for monthly evidence as a minimum and a sampling protocol for inspection rights.

Can you propose language or a schedule we can include in the order form? Also looping in procurement for timeline.

Thanks,
James Sullivan
Head of Security Programs
Acme Health

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights / pen-test window for Redwood MSA

James — thanks for the clear asks. Quick read-through and proposed operational plan below; I've attached a short evidence matrix and a draft redline for the MSA/Order Form security exhibit.

Summary proposal (operational):
- Pen test windows: We can commit to quarterly 2-week staging windows; Redwood requires 10 business days' notice and an ops-approved test plan. Tests will be limited to staging; production testing prohibited.
- Sampling & inspection: We propose a sampling approach vs full inspection: Redwood will provide monthly SOC 2 evidence snapshots (system config and control output for requested assertions) and will agree to one sampling inspection per 12 months with up to 10% of transaction/log sample size unless a security incident triggers broader access.
- Evidence handback cadence: Monthly automated snapshot (S3 link or secure Share), ad-hoc pulls for scoped inspections within 5 business days, and a 30-day window for remediation evidence.
- Access model: Staging access via a shared bastion/jump host and timeboxed credentials; all sessions logged. For pen-tests, agents must use a pre-provisioned staging environment; no VPN into customer production.

Next steps: legal redlines below (high-level) and I've dropped the draft redline file as "redline-proposal-msa-orderform.docx". Karthis and Laura — can you weigh in on (a) the 10-day notice and (b) the 10% sampling cap?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: pen_test_scope_v1.pdf, evidence_matrix_v2.xlsx, redline-proposal-msa-orderform.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, James Sullivan <j.sullivan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights / pen-test window for Redwood MSA

Thanks Grace. A few legal points and suggested alternative phrasing for the MSA redline (high level):

1) Inspection / sampling language: 'Up to 10% of production logs/transactions' is risky as a hard cap — propose: 'reasonable sampling not to exceed 10% absent reasonable cause.' This preserves our ability to expand scope if the customer identifies credible issues.

2) Notice & scheduling: 10 business days' notice is acceptable for standard pen-tests. For red-team style or tests that simulate active exploitation, require 20 business days and coordination with Redwood Security with option to reschedule for critical infra upgrades.

3) Non-disruptive covenant: Keep a clear 'non-disruptive' clause and right to suspend tests that risk production. Be explicit about scope (staging only) and list forbidden activities (denial-of-service, social engineering against Redwood employees, privilege escalation into customer-managed infra).

4) Evidence exports: Don't commit to continuous live access to logs. Provide snapshots and scoped exports. For third-party auditors, require an NDA and mutually agreed statement of purpose; support for onsite or remote inspections is limited to the scope in the Order Form.

I've annotated the redline doc with in-line comments. Ben — please add any commercial guardrails (credits, SLO carve-outs) we should offer if tests are delayed or produce operational impact.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify audit rights / pen-test window for Redwood MSA

Adding technical constraints from security ops:

- Staging environments: We will provision a staging stack that mirrors production for the tests. It supports up to 3 concurrent test engagements per quarterly window.
- Rate limits & safe guards: Pen-tests must respect predefined rate limits; we will provide a target traffic profile and a kill-switch for the engagement.
- Evidence exports: We'll provide weekly snapshots for the month surrounding the test and will retain raw logs for 90 days on a secure, access-controlled bucket. For formal inspections, we can export scoped logs (redacted PII) within 5 business days.

Attachment: pen_test_scope_v1.pdf contains the ops checklist and pre-test checklist. James, please review the staging constraints — if you need broader coverage we'll need to sign off additional run-hours.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Ops | Redwood Inference

- For evidence snapshots, monthly snapshots + ad-hoc exports within 5 business days works for our compliance team.

Procurement: please proceed to incorporate the attached redline into the order form and advise if we need a short SOW for extended hours.
